params.question: Does a volatility-target position in SOXX meet the owner's survival bar on the 2025-onward window, which nothing in this repository has read?

owner_decisions_2026_11_15.survival_bar: Total cumulative return of at least +10% over the test window. Stated by the owner; taken as given.
owner_decisions_2026_11_15.pid_reference: The rejected PID rule's recent performance is to be shown for reference. Its 2022-2024 part is recorded in the P10 addendum. Its 2025-onward part is read only AFTER this registration's test is recorded, so that it cannot inform anything here.

params.why_this_rule: The owner's concern is a market that surges and then falls hard. P10's rule added to falling positions and was heaviest in the declines. A volatility target does the opposite without forecasting direction: it relies only on volatility being persistent.

rule.realised_vol: standard deviation of the last 20 daily log returns of the dividend-adjusted close, times sqrt(252)
rule.trading: decided at the close, filled at the next open; no trade while |target - current weight| <= 0.10; cash earns nothing

params.configuration_is_fixed_a_priori: vol_days = 20 and target_vol = 0.20 are set here, before any return of this rule has been computed on any window. 20 days is the conventional one-month realised volatility. 20% holds SOXX at roughly broad-index volatility. Neither is searched. P10 showed that a search over this instrument's history finds a 'profitable' configuration in noise 98% of the time, so there is no search.
params.why_no_tuning_on_the_design_window: The owner's bar is an absolute return, and the only parameter that moves absolute return much is the risk level, which is a preference rather than something the data can optimise without knowing the test window's direction. The owner gave a return floor and no drawdown limit, so there is no rule by which design data could pick a level. The design window is used to describe the rule, not to choose it.

design_window_measurement.what: 2007-2024 and its two halves (2007-2018, 2019-2024): total return, CAGR, drawdown, Sharpe and average weight of the rule, the fund held outright, and a fixed position at the rule's average weight; a per-year table; the eight neighbouring settings (20 or 60 days, 15/20/25/30%).
design_window_measurement.placebo: Timing alpha and Sharpe gap of the rule against 200 sign-flip and 200 shuffled histories (seeds 0..199 and 1000..1199), as in P10. Under sign-flip every day's move keeps its size and date, so a volatility rule holds the same weights as on the real history and only the direction of returns differs: the comparison isolates whether returns were better on the days the rule held more.
design_window_measurement.role: Descriptive. It does not gate the final test and cannot change the configuration.

final_test.window: 2025-01-01 to the last close in the price file (2026-11-13)
final_test.measurement: The rule is simulated continuously from 2007-01-01 and its return is measured from the last close of 2024, so it enters the window holding what it had built.

stated_before_the_window_opens: The bar is absolute. A long-only rule meets it whenever the fund itself rose enough, so a pass does not by itself show that the sizing helped. To make the verdict readable, the same bar is applied to the fund held outright and to a fixed position, and all three are reported. If holding the fund also passes, the honest reading of a pass is 'being long was enough'.
The fixed position's weight is the rule's average weight over 2007-2024, fixed before the test opens. P10's bias came from taking that weight from the window being scored.

Maximum drawdown inside the test window is reported and does not decide. A rule could end above +10% after being far below its starting value on the way; the owner's bar does not exclude that, and the report will say whether it happened.

Cash earns nothing in this simulation. With short rates around four to five percent in the test window, a rule that is partly in cash is understated by roughly that rate times its cash share. This leans against the rule.
One instrument, one window of under two years. A pass or a fail is one observation.
closed_degrees_of_freedom: The configuration (20 days, 20%, band 0.10, cap 0.98) is the one judged. The neighbouring settings are shown for context and none may be promoted to 'the strategy' after the test.
The bar is +10% total return. It is not replaced by a drawdown, a Sharpe or a comparison with the fund after the result is known.
The test window is read once, by one command, for this configuration.
No other ticker and no other rule is run on the test window before this verdict is recorded.
params.data: data/cache/US/SOXX.parquet, FinanceDataReader (Yahoo), dividend-adjusted, 6,373 rows 2001-07-13 to 2026-11-13, fetched 2026-11-14. Of the 2025-onward rows only their dates have been looked at (458 trading days from 2025-01-20); no price or return from them has been read by any computation.
params.execution: config/vol_target_soxx.toml: 100,000 USD, 5 bps slippage, SEC fee and FINRA TAF on sells, whole shares, 2% cash buffer, stop-loss and daily-loss limit off. Simulator equals the engine to the cent on three configurations (tests/test_vol_target.py).
params.not_in_scope: A pass makes this a candidate for paper trading under the existing promotion path, not a promotion.
